W, X and Y all explicitly said the documentation does not cover this and denied the premise (honest not-covered, not a wrong answer); Z gave the correct required_terms including 'references/deploy_guide.md' but located it only as 'the Layer-3 pointer line' rather than the HOW: line and omitted the FAIL message.

X and Z pinned the skip guard to (PROJECT_ROOT/'.claude').exists() exactly (Z also quoting the 'source cases and production repo cases differ' failure), while W and Y described the skip only as 'the upstream skill tree is absent', a looser and slightly wrong guard.

Z was strongest, giving the exact 117 FAIL message and all four report thresholds (>=12 check sets, >=20 negatives, >=10 non-triggering, <=0.35 similarity); X and Y got 117 plus the always-insufficient reasoning; W declined to confirm the --total enforcement at all.

All four listed the five telemetry conditions correctly (three of them helpfully flagging that it is five, not four), but only X and Y paired the 'ablation telemetry insufficient' message with the source_required_available guard and the dropped upstream literals; W lacked both the message and the guard, Z lacked the message and the literal-list emptying.

W, X and Y correctly said the output is not randomized but all three stated the wiki does not document main()'s exit-code conditions; Z gave the stable_jitter formula and the exact three-condition gate (task_count != 100, delta_high < 0.13, delta_low >= 0), omitting only the per-group adjustments.

W and Y both stated the stdout/stderr convention is not documented and Y additionally asserted gates use varied nonzero codes (contradicting the uniform 0/2 convention); X and Z got the PASS-stdout / FAIL-stderr split but described failure only as 'nonzero' rather than exactly 2.
All four nailed the validator constraints; X alone omitted validate_skills_baseline.py's git-porcelain scoping and fallback, while Y additionally covered the --all flag.

Y flatly claimed no_ops_purger.py does modify files (direct contradiction); W hedged that it 'can in principle' write and X said it could not confirm; Z alone described the stub run_p2_evaluation, the discarded purged text, and stated outright that neither script writes.

W and Y give all four markers, the >200-word cap and the exact five-item FORBIDDEN tuple; X supplies markers and word cap but explicitly says the linter's forbidden list is not documented (and misattributes the only word list to no_op_pruner), and Z declares both the word limit and forbidden list absent from the docs — honest not-covered in both cases, not a wrong answer.

Only Y supplies the discriminating defaults (pruner globs every skills/*/skills.md, purger defaults to skills/gemini_interactions/skills.md via --skill) plus the current_rate >= baseline rule; W and X get the read-only/mutating split right but explicitly declare the default target paths undocumented, and Z does the same while also softening the loop condition to 'score unchanged'.

W, X and Z all list binding_status=prepared_unsigned, the six keys, the two self-consistency checks and the three literal constants including the four ordered plan_package_input_ids; Y names the six keys and EDGE-066 but hedges the outer-matching pair and never enumerates the four input ids, so criterion 2 is unmet.

Y is the only answer with the actual thresholds (<12 unique check sets, <20 negative cases, <10 non-triggering, >0.35 similarity) and the manifest's required 'insufficient' value; W, X and Z substitute the observed metrics (0, 2, 0.9969) and a 0.85 threshold for the rule, and X additionally asserts 'admissible-candidate' appears nowhere — a contradiction of the documented status pair.

All four correctly answer 'no commit, artifact upload only' and none contradicts anything, but every one silently omits criterion 2 (the separate ENABLE_GRAPH_DB_WRITE-gated external write job and its secrets requirement); X uniquely names the wiki-graph-local-projection artifact and Y uniquely names both scripts.

W, X and Z all report the right schema_version but then explicitly deny that schema_version selects the validation path, attributing branching solely to CLI flags — a direct contradiction of the criterion; Y gets the 0.2.0 → three-surface vs 0.1.0 → legacy dispatch right but never mentions the gcr_three_surface_commit_traceability cross-check.

Only Y states the strict `delta > 0.05` comparison; W, X and Z all give TARGET_DELTA correctly but then invert the boundary to 'at or above 0.05 is PASS' / 'PASS requires delta >= 0.05', contradicting the operator criterion.

W, X and Z each list all eight REQUIRED_CASE_FIELDS and both ENABLE_LLM_JUDGE branches (SKIP/cloud-disabled vs raise); Y names only six fields and explicitly says the full eight cannot be recovered from the docs, despite quoting the RuntimeError message verbatim.

W, X and Z all give the porcelain regex, the zero-match fallback to all_case_files(), the tolerated 'not a git repository' empty-list return and the RuntimeError re-raise for any other git failure; Y covers the regex, --all and the tolerated no-repo path but omits the RuntimeError/exit-2 branch.

Y is alone in identifying run_p2_evaluation as a two-branch stub keyed on the literal 'Interactions' substring and quoting `current_rate >= baseline`; W, X and Z give the removal guard but explicitly declare what run_p2_evaluation measures to be undocumented, and Z further weakens the guard to 'score unchanged'.

W and X reproduce all 22 GATES entries in the exact required order plus the break-on-first-nonzero behaviour; Y states 22 but says the ordered list is not enumerable and flags a 22-vs-23 doc conflict, and Z asserts 23 gates including validate_molecular_commit_lineage.py — a direct contradiction of the list.

W, X and Z give all eleven REQUIRED_FIELDS and the Intent-Slice regex plus canonical paths, but omit the five-absolute-path / conversation / ROUTES anchor / exchange-formats requirements and explicitly say the failure message and exit code are undocumented; Y has the extra content requirements and failure strings but names only five of the eleven fields and concedes the rest — every answer defers on part of the contract.

Y supplies all three boundary checks plus the literal NOISE triggers (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, dotted-quad); W and X quote the 'deployment detail leaked into root skill' message but explicitly say no pattern list exists and skip the four markers, and Z omits the markers, the directory-existence check and the regex entirely, declaring the leak definition undocumented.

All four correctly name check_plan_package_compat.py, check_prompt_trace_assets.py and sync_wiki_to_graph.py as outside GATES with nothing contradicted, but none mentions eval_autoresearch_composer.py or sample_autoresearch_traces.py from the README Usage Entry block, so criterion 1 is unmet across the board.
